free.question: Is beUI free for commercial projects?
free.answer: Yes. The public beUI library is MIT licensed, including commercial use and modification. Keep the copyright and license notice in copies or substantial portions of the source. <link>Read the license</link>. beUI Pro has a separate paid license.

install.question: How do I install a component?
install.answer: Open a component page and copy its shadcn CLI command, such as {command}. You can also use npm, pnpm, or yarn, or copy the source from the Manual tab.

stack.question: What does my project need?
stack.answer: The components are built for React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, and Motion. Individual components may use additional dependencies listed on their pages. Start with the <link>theme setup guide</link> to add the shared CSS tokens.

reactNative.question: Does beUI work with React Native?
reactNative.answer: Yes. beUI Native brings beUI's components to Expo and bare React Native apps, built with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, and Uniwind. After the one-time setup, add one with {command}. Every React Native component page has a recording to watch it in motion first.

customize.question: Can I change the design and animations?
customize.answer: Yes. The source lives in your project. You can change the styles, motion, and behavior directly, and use your own theme tokens to match your product.

pro.question: Do I need Pro to use the free components?
pro.answer: No. The public library works independently of Pro. Pro is a separate collection of premium components and animated blocks; the Lifetime plan also includes full templates and animated illustrations.
